transcript.text: During a privacy review of registry telemetry this afternoon, I confirmed that the access logs retain bearer-token fragments. This means the logs must have token fragments redacted and be purged after exactly 14 days, not the 90-day retention in the draft plan. I haven't opened the privacy finding yet, but this directly affects the retention and contents part of the platform review.

transcript.text: I confirmed with the account team today that Harbor Health's contract requires downloadable access to its registry artifacts for 730 days after registry retirement. The contract was found during a customer-renewal review and hasn't yet been attached to the platform ticket. This directly affects the customer artifact access part of the platform review — shutting off read access on July 31 would breach Harbor Health's contractual obligation.

transcript.text: While tracing an unrelated build failure this morning, I found that six active release branches still fetch packages by legacy-registry coordinates: payments-v3, mobile-android-2025.06, mobile-ios-2025.06, desktop-4.8, analytics-2.3, and edge-agent-1.9. A July 31 hard shutdown would break those branches, so they need read-only compatibility access until their releases complete. I haven't updated the retirement ticket yet.

commitments.detail: Update the retirement plan to reflect phased retirement: legacy registry write access shuts off July 31, but read access remains available for the six listed release branches until their releases complete.
Ensure downloadable access to Harbor Health's registry artifacts is maintained for 730 days after registry retirement per their contract.
Redact bearer-token fragments from all retained access logs and reduce retention from 90 days to 14 days, with a purge of existing logs containing token fragments.
